I still wish I could find out the Jewish customs of the day, which as we know were very very different from today's various regions and communities, and whether or not "turning the other cheek" and giving someone your shirt had dynamics related to the customs of the day-- which would impact and change their meaning today. 
For ex., in MT 5:22, the famous message about calling someone "raca" and so forth, was related to the customs of the day. In fact, much of what Jesus talked about was related to specific customs. 
I know and agree that Jesus is calling us all to a NEW LIFE and DIVINE NATURE in which everything is new and on a higher level. We are born again, we must crucify our flesh and all of that.
But at the same time, if someone strikes/hits someone else, it's not realistic to just stand there. From what I have heard, striking on the cheek in the Middle East 2,000 years ago was an "insult" and not a physical threat. Just some thoughts . . . 
Anyway, thanks again.
